status: unrefereed research candidate; internal AI-assisted review only

target.citation: Sinha, Kumar, Athalye & Chaudhury (2025), IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 73, 2646-2659, Section II-A (open question on PnP-ISTA with kernel denoisers)

claims.statement: For n <= 3, irreducible symmetric nonnegative K with K_ii = 1, K_ij <= 1, and symmetric PSD B with Be = be, b > 0: PnP-ISTA P(t) = W(I - tB) and PnP-ADMM R(t) are Schur stable for all 0 < t < 2/rho(B), W = diag(Ke)^-1 K.
claims.dependsOn: Banerjee-Chaudhury Theorem 1.3 (a self-contained argument is also given)

claims.statement: A fixed strictly positive symmetric stochastic SPD A in R^{4x4} (B = A^2) and fixed stationary vector admit, for each 0 < t <= 1/2, a Gaussian kernel K_t with kappa_2(K_t) < 19.22 for which P_t and R_t have a real eigenvalue > 1.

For 0 <= eps <= 1e-4 and 0 < t < 2 the four-state family is Schur stable iff Delta(eps,t) > 0; unstable steps exist iff eps < eps_crit = 1.6946633e-5; first loss T_-(eps) = (968750/133) eps + O(eps^2); along eps = t/1e5 unstable exactly for 0 < t < t* = 0.53128532534...

For primitive reversible W with nonnegative eigenvalues, gap g and stationary ratio kappa_pi, both iterations are Schur stable when t rho(B) < min{2, g/(sqrt(kappa_pi) - g)}; the order g is sharp within the four-state family (constant off by about 8,640).

A fixed strictly positive symmetric circulant stochastic SPD A_c in R^{12x12} and Gaussian kernels with eps = t^2 give a real eigenvalue > 1 for both iterations exactly for 0 < t < t_c = 1.9157074941...e-4 (unique root of p in (0,2]).
Without unit diagonals a reversible positive kernel with fixed positive forward operator is unstable in dimension three on an interval (t_-, t_+); dimension three is minimal there.

Symmetric W with spectrum in (-1,1] and PSD B: P(t), R(t) Schur stable for 0 < t < 2/rho(B) iff ker(I-W) and ker B meet only in 0; symmetrically normalised irreducible kernels satisfy this when Be = be.
Excess spectral radius at most about 1.72e-5 per iteration (four-state) and about 3.6e-8 (circulant).
Whether some irreducible unit-diagonal kernel on four points is unstable at a step in (t*, 2).

scope: Instability results choose the kernel for each step; each fixed primitive kernel is stable for sufficiently small steps. Not the first disproof of Banerjee-Chaudhury Conjecture 1.1 (Patel's MathDB post). No imaging experiment.
